subtype: Approach: redraws the path when a delay appears and shifts resources [Revision]
passage:
Sabina: Your launch slipped once. How did you handle it?

Gopika: The security review we needed came back two weeks late. My first feeling was panic, honestly. Then I redrew the board and asked which tasks now decided the end date. Testing the checkout and the data move, because they waited on the review's answer. So I shifted two developers off the animations and the settings page and onto those two. Everything that could wait, waited: the dark theme, the help page, the extra language. People grumbled about the dark theme. I said it would go in the next release. We launched five days after the new date instead of two weeks.

Sabina: What would you do differently?

Gopika: Draw that board on day one.

qa.q: Which two tasks did the two developers move onto?
qa.a: The two developers moved onto testing the checkout and the data move.

qa.q: How did Gopika feel at first when the review came back late?
qa.a: Gopika felt panic, honestly, at the start.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Gopika's story, and why did it help?
qa.a: Gopika redrew the board to see which tasks now decided the end date, then moved people to them, so the delay shrank.

qa.q: How might the people who wanted the dark theme have felt?
qa.a: They grumbled, and may have felt their work was being set aside, until they heard it would go in the next release.

grounding: Shows a lead redrawing the path after a delay and moving developers to the tasks that now determine the end date.
